text:
Kirby Dach has had a rough few years with injuries, so a healthy, productive stretch counts for something. He has seven points in 18 games, and Habs Eyes on the Prize recently wrote that he's finding his form. He scored in two of Montreal's last four wins. There's also a trade angle: The Sick Podcast's Lariviere argues he's building his trade value.

He's playing just over 11 minutes a night, mostly third-line work, and the numbers look like a solid depth player. His scoring rate, 2.07 points per 60, is above last season's 1.78, his finishing is fair (2 goals on 2.6 expected), and Montreal takes 51% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, about the team rate. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking suggests his value doesn't come from creating offense at five on five.

The third overall pick in 2019 hasn't become the player that pick promised, but our talent range has him at about 32 points over a full season, which is useful. Our model's closest comparison is Nils Hoglander. Watch his minutes while Montreal's lineup is thin.
